node_definition.done_when: A test queues a three-section chain in one call and the sections launch in dependency order as each upstream promotes, with no coordinator call in between; a negative arm marks the middle section's upstream abandoned, and the tail goes blocked-upstream and never launches; a malformed node in the same batch is refused at queue time. Readiness is read through the derivation roadmap uses, imported rather than re-implemented. The two new states are defined in reckon/crew/queue_admission.py beside QUEUED_PHASE, and every phase filter reads them from there. On the base commit the chain's later sections launch at once, ignoring their waits, so the test fails there. Gate: tests/test_a_queued_request_waits_on_its_dependencies.py tests/test_a_queued_run_is_admitted.py tests/test_a_queued_run_keeps_one_id.py tests/test_crew_obligations.py plus every existing test module that imports reckon/crew/queue_admission.py, reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py or reckon/crew/dispatch.py, named in the manifest, and tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py. The width test's reckon/roadmap.py failure is pre-existing on main. Run the gate in the foreground on the fleet allocation, with the revision, tree and command on the log's first line; ruff check and ruff format --check report nothing added on the staged paths.
